index.flow.heading: From first message to result in three steps
index.flow.1.p: Tell us what the company does and what you need. No ten-page brief.
index.flow.2.p: We tell you which line fits (outbound, a site, video or a mix) and whether any does.
index.flow.3.p: Every message is written for one company from verified facts about it. You see work in progress, not just the final result.
index.hero.tagline: We open the doors. Closing is still yours to do.
index.hero.lede: Cold emails usually end up in spam not because the product is bad, but because they were copy-pasted at two in the morning. We find the companies that genuinely have a reason to listen, vet each one as if we were about to work there ourselves, and open the conversation in a way that's actually worth answering.

index.situation.heading: The product is ready. Barely anyone finds out about it on their own.
index.situation.body1: At an early stage the founder almost always closes deals personally, and rightly so: nobody knows the product better. But there's an hour, maybe two, left for cold outreach between investor calls, hiring and putting out fires. That hour usually goes to scrolling LinkedIn, not to doing the work systematically.
index.situation.body2: We take exactly that hour (sourcing, vetting, first contact) and hand it back as someone on the other end of the conversation who's actually ready to talk. Closing stays with you: it's still the one part not worth outsourcing.
index.svc.outbound.title: Outbound
index.svc.outbound.body: Not five hundred addresses and a prayer. Companies that genuinely have a reason to hear you out, found, checked against the registry and their website, and opened for conversation with a personal message.
index.svc.sites.title: Websites
index.svc.sites.body: A marketplace listing isn't a website. It's a place a customer never visits twice. We build the thing that makes them stay a minute longer.
index.clientsteaser.heading: Who we already work with
index.clientsteaser.body: The list is short not because we lack offers, but because we say no more often than yes. The Clients page covers exactly what we do for the ones who made the cut.
index.close.heading: Tell us what the company does
index.close.line: No ten-page brief, no introductory call required. Describe the product and your current clients in a couple of messages, and we'll tell you honestly which line of work fits, and whether any does.
index.close.alt: Response within one business day, on any channel

services.au.heading: Your site loses leads quietly. We'll show you exactly where
services.au.lede: We look at your site the way a new client and a search engine do: speed, mobile, SEO, copy, the path to a lead, and trust signals. You get a list of problems ranked by importance, and what to do about each one.
services.au.inc.heading: From a free review to a work plan
services.au.inc.express.body: The 5-7 biggest problems on a single page. Free, so you see how we work before you pay anything.
services.au.inc.full.body: Every area: tech, SEO, offer, conversion, trust, link previews on social media. 15-40 items, prioritised.
services.au.inc.plan.body: The full report plus a step-by-step fix plan with timing and cost. We can fix it ourselves, or you can hand the report to your developer.
services.au.s1.title: A link
services.au.s1.body: Send us the address and a few words about who your clients are. No access to the site needed.
services.au.s2.title: Review
services.au.s2.body: We open the site on a phone and a laptop and check speed, indexing, titles and descriptions, copy, forms and contacts.
services.au.s3.title: Report
services.au.s3.body: Every item: what's wrong, why it costs you clients, how to fix it, and how urgent it is.
services.au.s4.title: Fixes
services.au.s4.body: If you like, we fix it ourselves. If not, the report is yours, and any developer can work from it.
services.au.std.heading: Conclusions, not a tool dump
services.au.std.1: An eighty-page report of automated checks without a single conclusion
services.au.std.2: Advice to "redo everything" where three fixes would do
services.au.std.3: A hidden condition that the fixes must be ordered from us
services.au.std.line: A good audit takes ten minutes to read, and you can start fixing things the same day.
services.at.heading: A lead shouldn't get lost between the site, the inbox and a notebook
services.at.lede: Telegram bots and connections between tools for small teams: leads land in a spreadsheet or CRM on their own, the client gets an instant reply, and you get a notification on your phone.
services.at.inc.heading: Three kinds of routine you can hand to a machine
services.at.inc.bots.body: Lead capture, bookings, catalogue, FAQ answers, payments. The bot replies at night and on weekends.
services.at.inc.integr.body: Site form Google Sheet or CRM Telegram notification. No manual copying, no lost leads.
services.at.inc.data.body: Competitor prices, new leads, stock levels: collected from sites and tools and sent to a sheet or chat on a schedule.
services.at.s1.title: Review
services.at.s1.body: We look at how a lead or task moves today, and where it gets lost or eats up time.
services.at.s2.title: Plan
services.at.s2.body: A simple diagram: what we automate, what stays with people, and what it costs.
services.at.s3.title: Launch
services.at.s3.body: We build it, test it on real leads, and hand over access along with a short guide.
services.at.s4.title: Support
services.at.s4.body: We keep it running and extend it as you grow, on a monthly plan or one-off.
services.at.std.heading: Automation you don't depend on us for
services.at.std.1: A complex system where a single spreadsheet would do
services.at.std.2: Bots that pretend to be a real person
services.at.std.3: Setups that stop working without us: the code and access stay with you
services.at.std.line: The best automation is the one you only remember when a new lead shows up.
services.sm.heading: People check your social media before they reply to your email
services.sm.lede: After an email or a call, people open your Instagram, Telegram or LinkedIn. If the last post is a year old, the company looks closed. We run your accounts so they show what you're doing right now: projects, production, people, clients.
services.sm.inc.heading: Three parts of one job
services.sm.inc.plan.body: A monthly content plan for your goals and platforms. We write the copy ourselves, from facts about your work, with no generic lines about “quality and reliability”.
services.sm.inc.media.body: Photos and short videos: production, warehouse, sites, team. We do the editing ourselves, it's our Video line of work.
services.sm.inc.run.body: We post on schedule and reply to comments and messages by agreed rules. Questions about prices and orders go to you.
services.sm.s1.title: Review
services.sm.s1.body: Which accounts you already have, who your clients are and where they look for you. For B2B that's more often Telegram and LinkedIn than Instagram, and we don't open a platform for its own sake.
services.sm.s2.title: Profile
services.sm.s2.body: Header, bio, contacts, pinned posts. In ten seconds a visitor understands what you do and how to reach you.
services.sm.s3.title: Running
services.sm.s3.body: Posts on plan, a shoot once a month, replies. You approve the plan and the copy, we do the rest.
services.sm.s4.title: Report
services.sm.s4.body: Once a month: what went out, what was read and watched, how many inquiries came in. If a platform isn't working, we say so.
services.sm.std.heading: A living account, not numbers for their own sake
services.sm.std.2: Posts made of stock images and generated holiday greetings
services.sm.std.3: Promising sales from social media where clients come by referral
services.sm.std.line: The best post shows what you already do, and do well.
services.ph.heading: The first opens the door. The second makes sure there's something worth seeing behind it. The third makes it memorable.
services.ph.lede: Outbound earns you a conversation with someone ready to listen. A website holds their trust when they check you out themselves. Video shows the product in the one minute they're willing to give you. Social media keeps the company visible between deals. An audit shows where the site loses clients, and automation makes sure leads don't get lost afterwards. Separately, or together.
services.close.line: Describe the product and your current clients. We'll tell you which line of work fits, and whether any does.
services.vd.heading: Two seconds to avoid the swipe. The rest to get watched to the end
services.vd.lede: For companies with something to show but no time to sit in an editor: phone recordings, webinars, interviews, client testimonials, production footage. We turn it into videos that work on your site, on social media and in conversations with clients.
services.vd.inc.heading: We pick it up at any stage
services.vd.inc.edit.body: We shape raw footage into a story: cut what's unnecessary, keep the pace, add titles, subtitles and music. Cutdowns for Reels, Shorts and TikTok from one long video.
services.vd.inc.post.body: Color grading, noise and echo cleanup, stabilization, loudness leveling. Phone footage starts looking like it was shot on purpose.
services.vd.inc.make.body: Script, storyboard, motion graphics and product animation. When there's nothing to film or no time to, the video is built from graphics, screencasts and text.
services.vd.s1.title: The goal
services.vd.s1.body: Where the video will live and what the viewer should do after watching: write to you, buy, remember the name. That sets the length, format and the first two seconds.
services.vd.s2.title: Material
services.vd.s2.body: We go through what you already have. If something's missing, we'll say what to shoot on a phone or fill the gap with graphics.
services.vd.s3.title: Rough cut
services.vd.s3.body: We show the structure before polishing details. Changes at this stage are cheap and fast.
services.vd.s4.title: A final cut for every platform
services.vd.s4.body: Color, sound, subtitles, plus versions in the right aspect ratio: 16:9 for your site and YouTube, 9:16 for Reels and Shorts, 1:1 for the feed.
services.vd.std.heading: Effects are not a substitute for meaning
services.vd.std.1: Transitions and effects just to look “dynamic”
services.vd.std.2: A three-minute logo intro before anything important is said
services.vd.std.3: Music and stock footage you don't have the rights to
services.vd.std.line: A good video makes sense without sound. That's how most people watch it.
services.ob.heading: Find the needle, then check that it isn't hay
services.ob.lede: For companies where sales are still handled by the founder, squeezed between an investor call and an interview with a new hire, with no time left to search for clients systematically.
services.ob.s1.title: Find
services.ob.s1.body: Selection isn't based on a generic fit with the client profile, but on a specific signal of interest: an open role that explicitly points to growth or automation, a company that sells an adjacent service itself, a salary range that signals real investment.
services.ob.s1.fine: No signal, no inclusion. Even if the company technically fits by size and industry.
services.ob.s2.title: Vet
services.ob.s2.body: The legal entity is confirmed through the company registry when the name is ambiguous. We check for bankruptcy or liquidation risk, real company size, and that the contact channel actually belongs to this company, not a similarly named one.
services.ob.s2.fine: A company with unresolved uncertainty about its entity or risk doesn't make the final list, regardless of how strong the signal is.
services.ob.s3.title: Write
services.ob.s3.body: Each message is drafted separately for its company. The opening acknowledges the recipient's decision as serious before naming the problem, and frames it as a normal stage of growth, not an oversight. No direct pitch, no call-to-action for a call in the first message.
services.ob.s3.fine: Every message is read twice: will it land with a real person, and could it read as a criticism.
services.ob.s4.title: Open
services.ob.s4.body: Contact happens through whichever channel the company actually uses: Telegram, email, or a call built around real objections. One measured follow-up if there's no reply. Handoff happens the moment a lead is ready to talk.
services.ob.std.heading: The bar is stricter than it looks
services.ob.std.intro: In a typical search cycle, fewer than a third of the companies found pass vetting. The final list isn't padded with weak candidates to hit a number. If the bar isn't met, the report says so.
services.ob.std.excl.1: A role that's technically live but effectively archived
services.ob.std.excl.2: A legal entity that can't be confirmed with certainty among similarly named companies
services.ob.std.excl.3: A company that turns out to be part of a national chain or holding
services.ob.std.excl.4: A contact that belongs to a different, similarly named brand
services.ob.std.line: Fewer, but certain. Better than more, but approximate.
services.ob.wr.heading: Written separately for each company
services.ob.wr.avoid.2: Perfectly symmetrical sentences of equal length
services.ob.wr.avoid.3: Phrasing that implies the recipient missed something
services.ob.wr.avoid.4: A call ask in the first message
services.ob.wr.instead.1: Acknowledging the recipient's decision before naming the problem
services.ob.wr.instead.2: The problem framed as a normal stage of growth
services.ob.wr.instead.4: A different structure for every company
services.ob.ch.heading: Where we actually write and call
services.ob.ch.email: A more formal structure, a subject line with no corporate phrasing, meaning preserved even if the wrong person opens it.
services.ob.ch.tg: Shorter and livelier. The first message reads as an observation, not a pitch.
services.ob.ch.call.body: A script built around real objections, with its own branch for a gatekeeper.
services.ws.heading: Thirty seconds decide whether they trust you or close the tab
services.ws.lede: For companies with a product and clients already, whose only online presence is a marketplace listing or a social page. Someone who's heard of you googles the name ten seconds before deciding whether to write to you at all.
services.ws.s1.title: Understand
services.ws.s1.body: What already exists: a social page, a marketplace listing, word of mouth. Who it sells to, and what a visitor looks for first, arriving from an ad or a referral.
services.ws.s2.title: Design
services.ws.s2.body: A structure built for one job: show the product and earn trust on the first screen, not ten “about us” sections that lead nowhere.
services.ws.s3.title: Fill in
services.ws.s3.body: Real copy and photos, no placeholders. Navigation that works well on a phone, because that's where most visitors come from.
services.ws.s4.title: Launch
services.ws.s4.body: Domain, hosting, basic analytics, plus an explanation of how to make small edits yourself afterward without calling a developer every time.
services.ws.std.heading: Speed without cutting corners
services.ws.std.1: A template thrown together in one evening without understanding the business
services.ws.std.2: Ten sections instead of one clear job for the visitor
services.ws.std.3: Design for its own sake at the cost of load speed on a phone
services.ws.std.line: The site has to sell in the first five seconds. Everything else is secondary.
services.ws.inc.heading: Three parts of one job
services.ws.inc.design.body: One screen, no scrolling, explains what the company does and why it can be trusted.
services.ws.inc.copy.body: Written for the specific product, not pulled from a generic “about us” template.
services.ws.inc.launch.body: Domain, mobile version, basic analytics. The site works from day one.
services.close.heading: Which line of work fits your case?
services.close.alt: Response within one business day, on any channel

clients.ph.heading: One client. Not for lack of offers.
clients.ph.lede: Outbound is daily manual work, not a “launch campaign” button. A fifth client at the same time simply wouldn't get the attention the first one does, so there isn't a fifth one yet. Below is who we work with right now.
clients.camirix.about: Camirix is a SaaS platform for sales automation and customer service: CRM analytics, AI lead qualification and AI Customer Support for growing B2B companies.
clients.camirix.scope.what.v: Daily sourcing and vetting of companies with a genuine signal of interest in sales automation, across 2-3+ industries per cycle.
clients.camirix.scope.icp.v: Growing B2B companies, 30-150 employees, $1-30M+ revenue, with an existing sales team and CRM.
clients.camirix.scope.deliver.v: Vetted companies with a contact and, where possible, a named decision-maker, a personal message for each, tracked in a shared database.
clients.camirix.note: Work runs every working day, and messages go out in the recipient's business hours. Lists aren't padded with weak candidates to hit a number. Some cycles end with a shorter list than the target, and the report says so plainly.
clients.fit.heading: Not built for every company
clients.fit.yes.1: The product is already selling, with confirmed clients
clients.fit.yes.2: Sales are handled by the founder or one person part-time
clients.fit.yes.3: You need a stream of real conversations, or a site worth trusting, not a report of work done
clients.fit.no.2: A sales team already exists and just needs more hands
clients.fit.no.3: The product hasn't sold to a single client yet
clients.close.heading: Tell us what the company does
clients.close.line: If the list above sounds like your situation, write in. We'll tell you honestly whether there's room, and what a list would look like.
clients.close.alt: Response within one business day, on any channel
